bindings.label: Rough sandpapery skin changes on the face present for 2½ years
A woman in her 70s with a history of polycythemia vera and acute myelogenous leukemia; the skin condition began before the AML diagnosis and hydroxyurea treatment.
The skin changes involved a rough sandpapery sensation without pruritus or pain, extending to the neck, upper chest, and bilateral forearms.

Physical examination showed background erythema with numerous rough horny spicules at the follicular ostia on the face, ears, neck, upper chest, and bilateral forearms, plus a pigmented macule on the right cheek.

Previous treatments with triamcinolone acetonide cream 0.1%, bacitracin ointment, and combination antibiotic ointment (neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B, and bacitracin) showed no improvement; daily medications included donepezil hydrochloride, melatonin, and aspirin 81 mg.
Skin biopsy shows numerous mites in follicular infundibula with hyperkeratosis and lichenoid infiltrate
The skin condition is a mite-associated follicular dermatosis (Demodex folliculitis)
Patient has PV/AML-related immunosuppression from polycythemia vera, acute myelogenous leukemia, and hydroxyurea treatment
